questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Australia had always been a destination I wanted to experience, both academically and personally. Queensland University of Technology (QUT) offered relevant courses within my field of study, while Brisbane appealed to me because of its high quality of life, international environment, and proximity to nature and travel opportunities. The combination of academic quality, English-speaking culture, and the opportunity to experience a different part of the world were the most important factors in my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Has been an amazing experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, it was quite easy to find the information I needed. QUT provided clear communication before arrival, including information about enrolment, orientation activities, accommodation options, and practical matters. Most information was available online, and any remaining questions could easily be answered through student services or exchange coordinators.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, I received support through QUT’s orientation program, which included campus tours, information sessions, and opportunities to meet other exchange and international students. There were also dedicated staff members available to help with administrative questions, course registration, and settling into student life. This support made the transition much smoother.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the orientation and support provided by QUT. The university made a strong effort to help international students feel welcome and informed from the beginning. The orientation activities were useful both academically and socially, and the staff were approachable and helpful whenever assistance was needed. Overall, the support contributed positively to my exchange experience.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding off-campus housing in Brisbane was relatively straightforward, especially with the help of Facebook groups,
Flatmates.com.au
, and recommendations from other students. However, it is a good idea to start looking early, as the best and most affordable options can be taken quickly before the semester begins. I would recommend choosing accommodation close to public transport or within easy reach of the QUT campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should be aware that rental prices can be relatively high, particularly in popular areas close to the city centre. It is important to budget for additional expenses such as utilities and public transportation. Living off campus can be a great way to experience local life and meet both Australian and international students, but it requires a bit more independence and planning than living in student accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I was satisfied with the housing options available. There were many different accommodation types to choose from depending on budget and preferences. While finding the right place required some effort, I was able to find suitable housing that met my needs and contributed positively to my exchange experience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the registration process quite easy and well-organized. The university provided clear instructions throughout the process, and most steps could be completed online before the semester started.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process involved selecting courses, obtaining any necessary approvals, and enrolling through QUT’s online student portal. Information about deadlines, course availability, and enrolment procedures was communicated clearly by the university. The process was generally smooth and intuitive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Support was available through both the international office and academic advisors. Staff members responded promptly to questions regarding enrolment, course selection, and administrative procedures. There were also online resources and guides available to help students navigate the system.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all, or nearly all, of my preferred classes. The course selection was flexible, and there were enough alternatives available if adjustments were needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend reviewing course options early and discussing them with your home university before departure. It is also important to pay attention to enrolment deadlines and prerequisites. If any issues arise, contacting QUT’s support services early is helpful, as they are generally responsive and willing to assist.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the academic programme at QUT. The courses were well-structured, relevant, and engaging, and they provided a good balance between theoretical knowledge and practical application. The learning environment was supportive, and the lecturers were approachable and knowledgeable.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were academically challenging but manageable. Compared to UCPH, there was often a greater emphasis on continuous assessment through assignments, group projects, presentations, and quizzes rather than relying primarily on a final exam. This encouraged consistent engagement throughout the semester. The academic level was high, although I found the workload to be distributed more evenly across the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at QUT was generally more interactive and practical than at UCPH. Classes often included discussions, case studies, workshops, and group work, which encouraged active participation from students. Lecturers were highly accessible and placed significant emphasis on student engagement. Compared to UCPH, there was less focus on independent study and more structured learning activities throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Introduction to Law
- IP
- Competition Law
- Legal research

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend courses that combine academic content with practical applications and opportunities for collaboration with other students. One of the strengths of QUT is its focus on real-world cases, group projects, and industry relevance, which provides a different learning experience compared to many European universities.

I would particularly recommend courses that include project work, case studies, or interaction with local businesses and organisations, as these offer valuable insights into the Australian context and help students develop practical skills alongside theoretical knowledge. Additionally, courses with a diverse mix of international and domestic students are a great way to gain different perspectives and build connections during the exchange semester.

Overall, I would encourage future exchange students to choose courses that may differ from those typically available at their home university, as this is a unique opportunity to broaden both academic and cultural horizons.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The main unexpected costs were related to housing and general living expenses. Rent was higher than I initially expected, particularly for accommodation located close to the city centre or the university. In addition, expenses such as public transportation, social activities, domestic travel, and setting up accommodation (e.g., household items and deposits) added up over the semester. While none of these costs were unmanageable, they were important to account for when budgeting for the exchange stay.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Accommodation, eating out, and entertainment were generally more expensive than I expected compared to Denmark. On the other hand, some grocery items, especially locally produced food products, were reasonably priced. Travel opportunities within Australia and to nearby destinations were also affordable when booked in advance. Overall, Brisbane offered a good quality of life, but exchange students should be prepared for relatively high living costs, particularly regarding housing and leisure activities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: QUT offers a wide range of activities through student clubs, sports teams, and international student programs. There are regular social events such as BBQs, city tours, and cultural nights. Sports facilities and university teams make it easy to participate in activities like fitness classes, team sports, and recreational leagues. In addition, there are many events specifically aimed at exchange and international students, which help with integration and socialising.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would strongly recommend exploring Brisbane and the surrounding areas, especially the beaches, national parks, and weekend destinations like Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast. Joining student clubs and attending social events at QUT is also highly recommended, as it is the fastest way to build a network. Travelling within Australia is a unique opportunity during exchange and adds a lot to the overall experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Goldcoast, Moreton island, straddie, Sydney, Melbourne, Noosa

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to adjust to the local culture. Australians are generally very open and friendly, which made it easy to meet new people and feel welcome. However, it still took a little time to adapt to the more informal communication style and the academic expectations at university. Overall, the transition was smooth and positive.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and student societies early, as that is the easiest way to meet both local and international students. At QUT, attending orientation events and faculty-specific activities also helps a lot in the beginning. In addition, saying yes to informal invitations (BBQs, beach trips, group study sessions) makes it much easier to build friendships. Locals are generally friendly, but you often need to take the first step

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One challenge was adapting to the more informal and relaxed communication style in both academic and social settings. In university, expectations can sometimes be less explicitly stated than at UCPH, so you need to be proactive in asking questions. Another difference was the strong emphasis on continuous assessment and group work, which required adjusting study habits and coordination with others.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open-minded people in Brissy

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Choose your accommodation carefully – distance matters a lot in Brisbane. QUT has two main campuses (Gardens Point and Kelvin Grove), and commuting can take longer than expected. Living close to one of the campuses or near a major bus/train line makes a huge difference. Brisbane is quite spread out, so what looks “close” on a map can easily turn into a 45–60 minute commute each way.

The teaching style is more structured and continuous than at UCPH
At QUT, you usually have multiple assignments, quizzes, and participation requirements throughout the semester instead of one final exam. This means the workload is more evenly distributed, so it’s important to keep up from the beginning. The upside is that feedback tends to be quick and quite clear.


Take advantage of the social life and outdoor lifestyle – it’s a big part of the experience
Brisbane has a very active, outdoor-oriented student culture. There are lots of events for international students and plenty happening around campus. The weather makes it easy to be social and active (BBQs, beaches, weekend trips). Say yes to opportunities early on – that’s the fastest way to build a social network.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is helpful to plan your course selection carefully in advance, as some units at QUT can fill up quickly or have specific prerequisites. Also, make sure to familiarise yourself with the assessment structure early in each subject, as expectations can differ quite a bit from UCPH. Finally, budgeting is important — Brisbane can be relatively expensive in terms of rent and daily expenses, so it is worth sorting accommodation early.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was the combination of academic development and personal growth through living in a completely different environment. Meeting people from all over the world and becoming part of a very social and active student culture was a highlight. Being able to travel around Queensland and Australia alongside my studies also made the experience especially memorable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenge was adjusting to the different academic system and maintaining consistent study discipline throughout the semester. The continuous assessment structure meant there was always something due, which required good time management. Additionally, settling into a new city and building a social network from scratch took some time at the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
